result.title: A Large-Dimensional Analysis of Least-Squares Federated Learning via Generalized Total Variation Minimization
result.summary: Federated learning over decentralized networks inherently trades off the suppression of local finite-sample noise through collaboration against the bias that collaboration introduces between heterogeneous nodes. We study this tension by performing a large-dimensional analysis of Generalized Total Variation Minimization with least-squares models. Using tools from random matrix theory, we show that Lipschitz observations of the global GTVMin solution concentrate in large dimensions, universally for any underlying network structure. We provide exact analytic expressions for the asymptotically precise performance under both i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. Gaussian mixture distributions on a fixed network. For the latter, these expressions quantify how regularization balances local adaptation against collaboration. Our theoretical results are confirmed by experiments on synthetic and real-world data.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用随机矩阵理论对最小二乘联邦学习中的广义全变差最小化（GTVMin）做大维渐近分析，给出 i.i.d. 与非 i.i.d. 高斯混合下协作与局部适应的偏差—方差权衡的解析表达式。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究的是去中心网络上的联邦优化与正则化权衡，既不涉及视觉或多模态推理，也没有关于推理状态生成、证据使用或停止决策的具体线索，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
